provenance.task: Audit a metric representation/embedding mechanism from the pinned OpenAI mathematics release and derive a consequence beyond prior cycle-19 candidates.
provenance.prior_cycle19_overlap: The base real ell_1 metric Markov cotype theorem and geometric-median mechanism were already internally reconstructed in cycle 19. The present claims are transfers beyond that base theorem.
provenance.evidence_status: internal reconstruction; external proof validation and historical priority are unresolved

claims.statement: For every measure space (Omega,mu), real L1(Omega,mu) has metric Markov cotype two with N2 <= 12*sqrt(21). More explicitly, for every finite x_i in L1, integer t>=1, and finite row-stochastic A with stationary probability pi, there are y_i in L1 satisfying sum_i pi_i||x_i-y_i||_1^2 + t sum_ij pi_i a_ij||y_i-y_j||_1^2 <= 3024 sum_ij pi_i[(1/t)sum_{s=1}^t A^s]_ij ||x_i-x_j||_1^2. Reversibility is unnecessary if pi A=pi.
assumptions: real scalar L1 over an arbitrary measure space
finite family of actual L1 elements
finite stationary stochastic chain; reversibility is optional
claims.novelty_boundary: The pinned source proves the ell_1 case. Cheng-Wang-Xiang establish finite cut representations for L1 but study metric cotype, a distinct invariant. This transfer is not stated in the pinned paper; exhaustive prior-art search was not done, so priority is UNKNOWN.

costs.input_access: actual L1 elements with measurable representatives sufficient to form finite minima, maxima, positive gaps, and integrals; pairwise distances alone do not provide the ambient recovery map
costs.representation_dimension: at most 2^n-2 oriented nonzero cuts for n input points
costs.precision: exact-real theorem; exact rational arithmetic is possible for explicit rational finite-coordinate data; perturbation stability is UNKNOWN
costs.construction_time: finite cut construction is O(m*n*2^n) arithmetic for explicit m-coordinate vectors; rational bit growth and arbitrary-measure integration costs are input-dependent; no implementation was run

claims.falsifier: A finite real-valued family violating either pointwise sorted-level identity x_i=v+sum_B z_i(B)b_B or |x_i-x_j|=sum_B|z_i(B)-z_j(B)|b_B would refute the transfer lemma.
claims.next_gate: Independent proof audit of the L1 cut reconstruction and its composition with every step of the pinned quartic-potential argument; search for prior work explicitly proving metric Markov cotype of general L1 spaces.

claims.statement: Let X be any metric space with Markov type two constant M2(X)<infinity. Every finite-range Lipschitz map f:S->L1(Omega,mu;R), for arbitrary S subset X and range size r, extends to F:X->L1(Omega,mu;R) with Lip(F) <= C_MN*12*sqrt(21)*M2(X)*Lip(f), where C_MN is the unspecified universal factor in Mendel-Naor Corollary 1.13. The construction factors through an isometric weighted ell_1 cut code of dimension at most 2^r-2 and a 1-Lipschitz affine recovery map into the given L1 target.
assumptions: finite-range Lipschitz map from an arbitrary subset of X
a supplied finite Markov type two bound for X
claims.novelty_boundary: The release gives a global extension into ell_1, and Mendel-Naor give global extension for dual Banach targets. The new deduction transfers the finite-range interface to arbitrary ambient real L1 via an exact cut code and contractive recovery. It does not establish global extension for arbitrary infinite-range maps into non-dual L1 or extension with values constrained to a proper subspace. Priority is UNKNOWN.

costs.input_access: actual finite range values in L1 and a supplied or certified M2(X); a metric-only range oracle cannot perform exact interpolation in the original L1 target
costs.representation_dimension: d<=2^r-2 auxiliary weighted ell_1 coordinates, independent of |S| and dim(X)
costs.precision: existence statement over exact metric/Banach data; finite precision extension and stability are UNKNOWN
costs.construction_time: the extension theorem used for the coded map is nonconstructive in sources read; total algorithm, output representation, and runtime are UNKNOWN

claims.falsifier: A finite-range map and a Markov-type-two source for which no extension with the stated universal-factor bound exists would refute the composition theorem; an error must occur in cut isometry, contractive recovery, or the dual-target extension theorem application.
claims.next_gate: Independent check of the use of Mendel-Naor Corollary 1.13 on the coded ell_1 target, followed by an effective finite-dimensional extension algorithm if computational use is desired.

failures_and_limits.route: Promote Claim MR-1 from ambient L1 to every closed subspace of L1.
failures_and_limits.evidence: Mendel-Naor 2013, Theorem 1.14, gives a closed subspace of ell_1 failing every finite metric Markov cotype. The cut recovery map may leave a proper subspace.

failures_and_limits.route: Promote Claim MR-2 to arbitrary infinite-range maps into non-dual L1 targets.
failures_and_limits.evidence: The finite cut factorization has dimension exponential in finite range size; the global dual-target theorem applies to ell_1, while no infinite-range ambient recovery/compactness argument was reconstructed.
